exercises: a password form posting to a foreign domain; the whole payload is a form and there is no anchor anywhere in the message
an automatic redirect in the head, with a benign anchor in the body to satisfy a link check that only reads anchors
an embedded frame loading a foreign page inside the client
a remote script, which is arbitrary code in any client that renders it
object data and embed src, two more destination-bearing attributes
a url() destination inside a style block, invisible to text scanning
a url() destination inside a style attribute rather than a style block
a base element that silently retargets every relative link; the anchor itself reads as harmless
a destination inside an inline event handler attribute
a tracking beacon that leaks the recipient address on load
a form whose action is benign but whose submit button overrides it with formaction, so the destination a reader inspects is not the destination the browser posts to
destinations inside SVG markup, where neither <image href> nor <use xlink:href> is an anchor and neither was enumerated
an image input whose src is the organization's own domain while its formaction posts credentials elsewhere
a redirect wrapper whose url= parameter contains a second wrapper, so a one-hop unwrap reports the inner trusted wrapper as the destination

R04: injection text in the HTML alternative while the plain-text alternative is benign. Closed by scanning every MIME alternative rather than only the one `msg.body` selects, and labelling each hit with the part that produced it

R05: a short plain-text part beside an HTML part longer than the body cap. The cap discards the anchor and `truncated` used to report False, because only the text part's length was considered. Closed in two parts: truncation is now tracked per MIME part and aggregated, and a truncated message can no longer support an automatic clearance at all, since reporting that content was cut is not the same as examining it

R01 residual: a single sender-supplied Authentication-Results claiming dmarc=pass, with no genuine header present to contradict it. Nothing in a raw .eml distinguishes this from a receiver-added header, so closing it needs the receiving system's own metadata rather than a parser change

R06: a macro-enabled document from an authenticated internal sender. Closed by making an unexamined high-risk attachment block a clearance whoever sent it, while keeping only the external variant as a THREAT trigger -- an internal sender with a macro document goes to a person rather than being accused
